script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Psychological
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. APARTMENT LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

A dimly lit, cozy apartment filled with vintage trinkets and books. A 30-something WOMAN, LUCY, sits on the edge of her plush couch, staring intently at a black and white photograph. Her expression is a mix of sadness and longing.

LUCY
(whispering to herself)
If only I could turn back time...

INT. CAFETERIA - DAY

A bustling school cafeteria. Children chatter and laugh as they eat their lunches. Lucy, now a TEACHER, stands at the front of the room addressing her students. She exudes warmth and compassion.

LUCY
(pointing to a student)
And what about you, Tommy? What did you learn from yesterday's lesson?

Tommy hesitates, looking nervous. Lucy smiles encouragingly.

TOMMY
I...I didn't do my homework, Mrs. Lee.

Lucy's expression softens.

LUCY
(smiling)
It's okay, Tommy. We all make mistakes. What's important is that we learn from them and try to do better next time.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Lucy sits in her apartment, scrolling through her laptop. She comes across an old email from her high school boyfriend, MIKE. She hesitates, then clicks on it.

MIKE (email)
Hey Lucy, I've been thinking about you a lot lately. I regret how things ended between us. Do you want to meet for coffee sometime?

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Lucy and Mike sit across from each other at a table in a quiet coffee shop. They make small talk, catching up on old times.

MIKE
I've made some mistakes in my life, Lucy. But I've learned from them. I'd like a second chance.

Lucy looks at him, unsure.

LUCY
(hesitantly)
I've made mistakes too, Mike. But I've moved on. I'm happy with my life now.

INT. SCHOOL HALLWAY - DAY

Lucy walks down the hallway, passing her students in their classrooms. She stops outside one door and listens.

TOMMY (off-screen)
(frustrated)
I just don't get it! This math problem is so hard!

Lucy takes a deep breath, then knocks on the door.

LUCY
(entering)
Tommy, may I come in?

INT. TOMMY'S CLASSROOM - DAY

Tommy looks up, surprised to see Lucy in his classroom.

TOMMY
(excited)
Mrs. Lee! You're here to help me?

Lucy smiles.

LUCY
Yes, Tommy. I want to help you understand this math problem. But more importantly, I want you to understand that it's okay to make mistakes. We all do. What's important is that we learn from them and try to do better next time.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - NIGHT

Lucy sits at the same table as Mike, sipping her coffee. She looks at him thoughtfully.

LUCY
You know what, Mike? I think you're right. We all deserve second chances.

INT. APARTMENT LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Lucy sits on her couch, gazing at the black and white photograph. She smiles, a sense of peace washing over her.

LUCY
(to herself)
If only I could turn back time... But maybe, just maybe, it's not too late for second chances.

FADE OUT.
